canonical_name: Blackdog Data Centre and AI Campus
summary: Proposed 'multi-gigawatt' hyperscale AI data centre campus on around 200 acres at Blackdog, five miles north of Aberdeen, including a former MoD firing range, announced in April 2026 by Ashfield Land and TechRE with an initial 600 MW phase claimed. No data-centre planning application has been lodged: the 'planning consent already secured' claim rests on a 2016 planning permission in principle (APP/2016/0766) for a mixed-use town centre/business scheme, with which the developers say the data centre plans would align. Powering the site from offshore wind (ScotWind/INTOG, Cerulean Winds' Aspen) via private wire is described as under discussion, not contracted.
maturity_explanation: Land assembled by the developers and a prior planning permission in principle (APP/2016/0766, mixed use, not a data centre) exists on the site, but no data-centre application, EIA screening/scoping or PAN has been located on the Aberdeenshire portal or in reporting; APRS and press state detailed planning is yet to be submitted. Announcement stage with claimed 'planning foundations' — early development, not M2/M3 for the data centre itself.
anticipated_construction_start: 2026 (developer hope, 'first ground broken', subject to final commercial agreements)

phases.description: Initial 600 MW of 'renewable and grid connected power'; developers state planning consent 'already secured' for the first phase, apparently relying on the 2016 mixed-use PPiP rather than any data-centre-specific permission.
Aspiration to scale to a multi-gigawatt data centre and AI campus; no capacity figure, application or grid evidence located for this ambition.

latest_development.headline: Developers Ashfield Land and TechRE announce 600 MW initial / multi-gigawatt data centre and AI campus at Blackdog, citing existing first-phase consent and hoped 2026 start

unknowns: Formal decision date, conditions and any section 75 obligations of PPiP APP/2016/0766 (Aberdeenshire Idox portal unreachable during research; committee approval 27 Apr 2017, ministerial clearance 22 Aug 2017, issue of decision notice not confirmed)

Whether PPiP APP/2016/0766 remains extant (PPiP durations/lapse) and whether a data centre (likely Class 4/5/6 question) genuinely falls within its terms — only the developers' own statement that plans 'would align' exists

Any grid connection application/offer with SSEN Transmission or NESO for 600 MW import — no evidence found beyond developer statements
Whether any contractual arrangement exists with Cerulean Winds (Aspen) or any ScotWind/INTOG project — reported only as 'discussions' and 'exploring'
Operator or anchor tenant — none named
